claims.text: Controlled thermal annealing can reduce the fraction of high-angle grain boundaries in Q235 steel while minimizing overall grain growth.
Reducing the fraction of high-angle grain boundaries will delay localized pitting-corrosion onset in Q235 steel exposed to 3.5% NaCl.
Reducing the fraction of high-angle grain boundaries will lessen pitting-corrosion severity in Q235 steel exposed to 3.5% NaCl.
The proposed corrosion benefit will occur at both room temperature and 60°C.
High-angle grain boundaries are high-energy boundaries.
High-energy, high-angle grain boundaries in Q235 steel preferentially act as sites for anodic dissolution.
Reducing high-energy, high-angle boundaries produces a more uniform grain-boundary network.
A more uniform grain-boundary network is less susceptible to localized corrosion initiation.
The annealing benefit will be more pronounced at 60°C than at room temperature.
Unintended grain growth or precipitate formation during annealing could affect corrosion behavior.
EBSD can be used to assess grain-boundary character distribution and grain size in the treated and untreated specimens.
The controlled study compares annealed Q235 steel with an untreated as-received Q235 reference in 3.5% NaCl at room temperature and 60°C.
The proposed response variables are time to corrosion initiation, pit density, and pit depth.
